_comment: Which long dash characters a catalog is allowed to contain, per language.
The house rule is that no shipped English string carries a long dash: there is
always a way to write the sentence with grammar instead, so a dash is a choice and
the rule costs nothing. That escape does not exist in every language, so the rule
is a function of the language rather than a constant.
Source files are always read as English. Only ValheimBakaLoader/WebUI/i18n/<code>.json
is read under its own code.
Codepoints are written as U+XXXX. An empty list means no long dash at all.

_why.ru: U+2014 is required punctuation in Russian, not decoration: it stands in for the omitted copula, which is how Russian writes 'X is Y', and leaving it out is a grammatical error rather than a style choice. U+2013 is the standard separator between digits in a range.
_why.ja: U+2014 is the base character of the Japanese dash; the doubled form is ordinary prose punctuation.
_why.zh-Hans: U+2014 doubled is the Chinese em dash, ordinary prose punctuation with no substitute.
_why.zh-Hant: U+2014 doubled is the Chinese em dash, ordinary prose punctuation with no substitute.
